newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks up at close, lethargic action.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks up at close, lethargic action.

text.p: Share prices edged cautiously higher at Bombay bourses on Friday, with major players sitting on the sidelines ahead of the weekend, traders said.
"Dull trade was the highlight of the day's action contrary to expectations of fireworks taking place after better results announced by State Bank of India (SBI)," a local dealer said.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index ended 23.66 points, or 0.82 percent, higher at a provisional 2,894.68 in rangebound trade.
Trading activity focussed on shares of SBI after the firm announced a 179 percent jump in 1996/97 (April-March) net profit to 6.41 billion rupees just before close of trade on Thursday.
The stock closed 2.25 rupees higher at 218.50 at the BSE in volumes of over 4.6 million shares.
Market-favourite SBI met market expectations after showing a smart rise in its first half net profit, but traders said the initial cheer after the good results had subsided.
"Surprisingly, a lot of action expected in the SBI counter failed to come up," the dealer at the local brokerage added.
With foreign institutional investors' holding reaching the 20 percent limit in SBI, foreign funds cannot make fresh purchases in the stock, traders said.
After close of trade, state-run Bharat Heavy Electronics Ltd (BHEL) said its first half 1996/97 net profit rose 41 percent to 687.2 million rupees against 486.8 million a year ago.

BHEL was up 5.50 rupees to 196.0 rupees, ITC 3.0 to 280.0, Bajaj Auto 16.50 to 842.0, MTNL 1.0 to 215.50 and M&M 4.0 to 286.0. Reliance shares were unchanged at 180.75. TISCO fell 0.75 to 153.25, ACC 2.0 to 1,008.0 and Gujarat Ambuja 23.0 to 216.25
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 5.0 points, or 0.61 percent, to a provisional close of 830.0.
